answer: An honest agent files, waits, files again: ten returns, ten years, one name. Tax filing history reads that rhythm: returns filed every year for a decade, each return stamped by a revenue service keeping its own copies. The farm files differently - a hundred returns in a week, all new, all thin - and the grove is the thinness: a return with no prior year behind it stands out like a stranger at a family dinner. The velvet is the audit: this year is compared against the last nine, and a gap ends the application. The zenith is the decade of patience the farm must buy, one year at a time.
